source.data:
# Changelog

All notable changes to fastqueue are documented in this file.
The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the project uses semantic versioning.

## [2.5.0] - 2026-08-19
### Added
- `Queue.drain(timeout=...)` returns all pending jobs without blocking workers.
- Redis backend: optional TLS client certificates (`ssl_certfile`, `ssl_keyfile`).
### Fixed
- Worker heartbeat no longer drifts under long garbage-collection pauses (#412).
- `fastqueue inspect` no longer crashes on jobs with non-UTF-8 payloads (#418).

## [2.4.1] - 2026-05-28
### Fixed
- Priority queues: jobs with equal priority are again served first-in, first-out (#391).
- Typing: `enqueue()` accepts `priority=None` again.

## [2.4.0] - 2026-05-06
### Added
- Priority queues: `Queue(priority=True)` and `enqueue(job, priority=0..9)` (#377).
- `fastqueue inspect --by-priority` shows queue depth per priority level.
### Changed
- The default retry backoff is now exponential with jitter (base 2 s, cap 5 min).
  Set `backoff="linear"` to keep the previous behavior.
### Deprecated
- `Queue.put()` alias. Use `enqueue()`.

## [2.3.2] - 2026-03-11
### Fixed
- SQLite backend: lock contention when more than 32 workers poll at once (#365).

## [2.3.1] - 2026-02-02
### Fixed
- Graceful shutdown waits for in-flight jobs up to `shutdown_timeout` (#352).

## [2.3.0] - 2026-01-14
### Added
- Scheduled jobs: `enqueue_at(when, job)` and `enqueue_in(delta, job)`.
- Prometheus metrics endpoint (`fastqueue worker --metrics-port`).
### Changed
- Minimum supported Python is now 3.10.

## [2.2.0] - 2025-10-30
### Added
- Dead-letter queue for jobs that exceed `max_retries`.
### Removed
- The deprecated `fastqueue.compat` module.

## [2.1.0] - 2025-08-21
### Added
- SQLite backend for single-host deployments.

## [2.0.0] - 2025-06-03
### Changed
- Jobs are serialized with msgpack instead of pickle. Pickled jobs from 1.x are
  not readable; drain 1.x queues before upgrading.
### Removed
- Python 3.8 support.

[2.5.0]: https://git.example.com/fastqueue/fastqueue/compare/v2.4.1...v2.5.0
[2.4.1]: https://git.example.com/fastqueue/fastqueue/compare/v2.4.0...v2.4.1
[2.4.0]: https://git.example.com/fastqueue/fastqueue/compare/v2.3.2...v2.4.0
